Optimal.Notes: The GoldSrc engine holds a rock-solid 60 fps at full native resolution and high detail with only 6 W TDP — a generous budget for a 1998 title. This is the recommended profile for the best balance of image quality, smoothness, and battery life.

profiles.Summary: Half-Life is a 1998 GoldSrc engine game with extremely modest hardware requirements, running effortlessly on the Steam Deck at maximum settings and a locked 60 fps with minimal power draw. It is Steam Deck Verified with full controller support, making it a near-perfect handheld experience.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's extremely modest 1998 PC requirements and the known behaviour of the GoldSrc engine on modern hardware. On first run, confirm the frame rate counter shows the expected numbers and verify controller bindings are working correctly in-game.

MaxBattery.Notes: At 4 W TDP and a low GPU clock, the GoldSrc engine barely taxes the Deck; even at Low detail the game looks essentially identical to its default appearance. The 40 Hz refresh with a 30 fps cap gives a smooth, tear-free image with maximum battery savings.

KnownIssues: Some players report minor audio crackling or desync under certain Proton versions; switching to Proton Experimental can help.
The in-game mouse sensitivity may feel off when using the right thumbstick; adjusting controller sensitivity in Steam Input is recommended.
Multiplayer (Half-Life Deathmatch) may require additional network configuration for some server browsers to populate correctly.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Uncapped frame rate with no TDP limit lets the engine run as fast as the hardware allows; the GoldSrc engine can push hundreds of fps, which benefits input latency in multiplayer. Battery life drops significantly with the APU unconstrained, so this profile is best for docked or plugged-in sessions.

Optimal.Notes: Native 1280x800 at maximum quality settings holds a rock-solid 60 fps with plenty of headroom; a 5 W TDP limit is more than sufficient for this engine. This is the recommended everyday profile.

profiles.Summary: Half-Life is a 1998 classic that runs effortlessly on the Steam Deck, well within the hardware's capabilities given its extremely modest system requirements. The game is Steam Deck Verified and runs natively through Proton with full controller support, delivering smooth performance even at the lowest power settings.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's 1998 GoldSrc engine requirements (far below Deck capabilities) and its Verified status. On first run, confirm the fps_max console variable matches your chosen cap, and check that controller bindings feel comfortable — adjust sensitivity in Options > Mouse/Keyboard if needed.

MaxBattery.Notes: At 3 W TDP this 1998 GoldSrc title runs locked at 40 fps with ease, delivering exceptional battery life. FSR upscaling from 960x600 is barely noticeable on the OLED panel at this game's art style.

KnownIssues: Mouse sensitivity may feel off with controller; use in-game sensitivity settings to tune
Multiplayer servers may require additional configuration or may have limited active population
Some older GoldSrc engine quirks (e.g. frame-rate-dependent physics) may surface at very high fps — capping to 60 is recommended

MaxPerformance.Notes: The GoldSrc engine has no trouble saturating 90 Hz on the OLED Deck; note that GoldSrc physics and some animations are tied to frame rate, so staying at a consistent cap (90) avoids oddities. Use +fps_max 90 in launch options to enforce the cap inside the engine as well.
